Week 6 · A1 · Beginner

Aller + infinitif

To talk about the future, use aller plus an infinitive: je vais manger (I’m going to eat).

Pick a person and a plan, then switch from “now” to “soon”. Watch aller arrive and the verb change into its infinitive.

aller (conjugated) + infinitive = the near future.

The futur proche works just like English “going to”: conjugate aller (to go) and add the verb in its dictionary form. Je mange (I eat) becomes je vais manger (I’m going to eat). It is the easiest way to talk about plans, and French speakers use it all the time. You also need three irregular verbs: aller, faire (to do, make) and venir (to come).

Pattern

Personallerfairevenir
jevaisfaisviens
tuvasfaisviens
il / elle / onvafaitvient
nousallonsfaisonsvenons
vousallezfaitesvenez
ils / ellesvontfontviennent

To say “not going to”, wrap aller: Je ne vais pas manger.

Examples

No French voice was found on this device, so the ▶ écouter buttons are hidden.

  • Je vais au marché. I’m going to the market.
  • On va manger ensemble ce soir ? Shall we eat together tonight?
  • Ils vont voyager en juillet. They’re going to travel in July.
  • Qu’est-ce que tu fais ce week-end ? What are you doing this weekend?
  • Elle vient de Dakar. She comes from Dakar.

Common mistakes

  • Je vais mange. → Je vais manger. The second verb stays in the infinitive.
  • Je vais à manger. → Je vais manger. No à between aller and the infinitive.
  • Vous faisez → vous faites. One of only three vous-forms without -ez (with êtes and dites).
  • Je ne vais manger pas. → Je ne vais pas manger. ne … pas wraps aller.

Quiz

Parler: your weekend

A1 goal: introduce yourself and talk about your day in short, simple sentences. Say four plans for this weekend with aller + infinitive: Samedi, je vais faire les courses. Dimanche, je vais appeler ma mère …
